message.content: {"summary":"An outstanding report. You identified several ethical issues and linked them clearly to engineering design, addressed both organisational context and stakeholder interests (Table 1), built balanced for/against arguments with rebuttals, and gave stakeholder-specific recommendations. Your evidence base is strong: eight reputable references and four external case studies with quantitative data (e.g., 81/236 NHS trusts, US$4.3B). Your structure and Figure 1 support the conclusion effectively. Only a minor format deviation: the abstract slightly exceeds the ~150-word target.","next_steps":["Trim the abstract to ~150 words by cutting background detail and keeping only purpose, method of argument, and conclusion.","Consider adding one more visual element type (e.g., a stakeholder-influence matrix) to further strengthen the discussion section.","In future work, push the 'against' arguments even further by quantifying the cost of delay, so both sides carry equal evidential weight."],"criteria":{"C1":"Excellent (10/10). You identified several ethical issues — test coverage set by schedule, the data-loss-as-harmless rule, and conflict of interest — and linked them to engineering design. Both organisational context and stakeholder interests are thoroughly addressed, with Table 1 clearly mapping stakeholders, stakes and decision power.","C2":"Excellent (10/10). Your for/against arguments are objective and deep, each rebutted, and you provide separate decision-making conclusions for Rachel, management, the health department, the chip supplier and the engineers — exceeding the stakeholder consideration the top level requires.","C3":"Excellent (10/10). The body follows a clear logical arc (for, against, decision rule, options, path), with Figure 1 supporting the reasoning. Your conclusion and Recommendations 1–5 flow directly from the arguments, and stakeholders without decision power are systematically considered.","C4":"Excellent (10/10). Eight reputable references (NAO, Leveson & Turner, HBR, DOJ, standards) combine quantitative evidence (81/236 trusts, US$475M, US$4.3B) with qualitative analysis across four external case studies, demonstrating balanced, in-depth research.","C5":"Excellent (10/10). Your writing is fluent and concise; abstract, introduction, body, conclusion and recommendations are all present and functional; two tables and a decision-flowchart figure are used competently; IEEE-style references are consistent and well matched to your arguments. Only the slightly over-length abstract deviates from format expectations."}}
